questions.label: Q1
questions.text:
Explain the difference between the error and the residual of an approximate solution $\tilde{x}$ to an equation of the form $f(x) = 0$.

Next, use two steps of the secant method to estimate the root of $f(x) = e^x - 3x - 1$ in the interval $[1, 2]$, starting at $p_0 = 1$ and $p_1 = 2$. Afterwards, compute $f(p_3)$, give the best bracket for the root that you have found, and give an estimate of the error.

questions.label: Q2
questions.text:
Use two steps of Heun’s third order method to estimate the solution of the initial value problem $\dot{y} = t - y^2$, $y(0.5) = 2.500$ up to time $t = 1.0$. You should aim to compute the solution using Heun’s method to an accuracy of at least 3 decimal places, and use sufficient precision in your working to do this.

Compare your answer with the exact solution, which has $y(1.0) = 1.32733490$ (8dp). What would you expect the absolute error to be if you were to use Heun’s method with 10 steps?

questions.label: Q3
questions.text:
Use divided differences to compute the cubic polynomial interpolating the following data:

| $i$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $x_i$ | 2.3 | 2.7 | 2.0 | 3.0 |
| $y_i$ | 0.60 | 0.23 | 0.98 | 0.06 |

Estimate the value of $y$ when $x = 2.5$. How does the ordering of the data points affect the interpolating polynomial?
questions.modelAnswer:
The divided differences are

| $i$ | $x_i$ | $f[x_i]$ | first | second | third |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 2.3 | 0.60 | | | |
| 1 | 2.7 | 0.23 | $-0.925000$ | | |
| 2 | 2.0 | 0.98 | $-1.071429$ | $0.488095$ | |
| 3 | 3.0 | 0.06 | $-0.920000$ | $0.504762$ | $0.023810$ |

Thus the Newton interpolating polynomial is

$$
p_3(x)=0.60-0.925(x-2.3)+0.4880952381(x-2.3)(x-2.7)+0.0238095238(x-2.3)(x-2.7)(x-2.0).
$$

At $x=2.5$:

$$
p_3(2.5)=0.60-0.925(0.2)+0.4880952381(0.2)(-0.2)+0.0238095238(0.2)(-0.2)(0.5).
$$

$$
p_3(2.5)=0.395.
$$

The ordering of the data points changes the divided-difference table and the Newton form of the polynomial, but it does not change the interpolating polynomial itself in exact arithmetic. With finite precision arithmetic, different orderings may give slightly different numerical round-off errors.

questions.label: Q5
questions.text:
The least-squares approximation to a function $f$ is given by $q_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^n c_k P_k(x)$ where the $P_k$ are the Legendre polynomials, and the $c_k$ are given by

| $k$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $c_k$ | 0.2267 | $-0.1341$ | $-0.0570$ | 0.0620 | $-0.0077$ | $-0.0122$ |

Use the recurrence relation to evaluate $P_k(x)$ for $k = 0, 1, \ldots, 4$ for $x = 0.3$, and hence compute $q_4(x)$. Compute the total square error $\int_{-1}^{+1} (q_2(x) - f(x))^2\,dx$, assuming $\int_{-1}^{+1} f(x)^2\,dx = 0.117242$ (6dp).

questions.label: Q6
questions.text:
Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&0\\0&1&2\\0&2&2\end{pmatrix}.
$$

After applying one step of the QR method we obtain

$$
A=QR=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&-0.4472&-0.8944\\0&-0.8944&0.4472\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3&0&0\\0&-2.2361&-2.6833\\0&0&-0.8944\end{pmatrix}.
$$

and

$$
A^{(1)}=R^{(0)}Q^{(0)}=RQ=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3.4000&0.8000\\0&0.8000&-0.4000\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Apply another step of the QR method to estimate the eigenvalues of $A$. Give bounds on the eigenvalues using the Gersgorin circle theorem.
questions.modelAnswer:
Apply QR factorisation to

$$
A^{(1)}=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3.4000&0.8000\\0&0.8000&-0.4000\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For the lower $2\times 2$ block,

$$
\left\|\begin{pmatrix}3.4\\0.8\end{pmatrix}\right\|=\sqrt{3.4^2+0.8^2}=3.492849839.
$$

One QR factorisation is

$$
Q^{(1)}\approx\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0.9734&0.2290\\0&0.2290&-0.9734\end{pmatrix},
$$

$$
R^{(1)}\approx\begin{pmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3.4928&0.6871\\0&0&0.5726\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Then

$$
A^{(2)}=R^{(1)}Q^{(1)}\approx\begin{pmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3.5574&0.1311\\0&0.1311&-0.5574\end{pmatrix}.
$$

The eigenvalue estimates from the diagonal are therefore

$$
\lambda_1\approx 3,
$$

$$
\lambda_2\approx 3.5574,
$$

$$
\lambda_3\approx -0.5574.
$$

Using Gersgorin circles on $A^{(2)}$ gives the intervals

$$
[3,3],
$$

$$
[3.5574-0.1311,3.5574+0.1311]=[3.4263,3.6885],
$$

$$
[-0.5574-0.1311,-0.5574+0.1311]=[-0.6885,-0.4263].
$$

Hence the eigenvalues lie in

$$
\{3\}\cup[3.4263,3.6885]\cup[-0.6885,-0.4263].
$$

questions.label: Q7
questions.text:
In a compartmental model of an infectious disease with two variants, individuals are either susceptible (S), infections with the first variant ($I_1$), or with the second variant ($I_2$). The progress of the disease is modelled by

$$
\dot{S}=-(\alpha_1 I_1+\alpha_2 I_2)S/N,\quad \dot{I}_1=\alpha_1 I_1S/N-\beta_1I_1,\quad \dot{I}_2=\alpha_2I_2S/N-\beta_2I_2.
$$

Assume initially 340 individuals infected with variant 1 and 1 individual infected with variant 2, in a population with size $N = 17\ 000\ 000$.

Show how to solve this system of differential equations in Matlab, including writing the code you would use.
